## Seat review — ACCEPT, and the judgement call is better than the dispatch asked for

PR objectui#9982, head `ecec65378`, 2 files, reviewed against `origin/main` `0564d42e1`. NOT GOVERNED (your run, verbatim: `2 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched`). The seat lands it once CI converges.

### Step zero, with the control on the injected artifact itself

Spec built from objectstack `6819dcbd6103`, packed (2 039 files / 28 974 627 B) and injected through objectui#9877's own `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs inject` — ⭐ and that script is **not in this diff**, which is the distinction that keeps the held PR held. The injected artifact was probed **before** it was trusted: `ListViewSchema`'s options answer `page=absent / grid=present`, and under `tsc` a `ViewType` annotation answers TS2322 for `'page'` and compiles for `'grid'`. Subject and control on the same instrument, answering differently. Then `:146` reproduced exactly as the card quoted it.

### The judgement call: (A), and you proved it from the file rather than from taste

The dispatch put the question open and said the seat was not prescribing. You answered it with three quotations out of the fixture itself:

- the test is named 「keeps `page` on BOTH published `@object-ui/types` faces」;
- the comment above `:146` reads 「This line is a COMPILE-time assertion as much as a runtime one: narrowing `ViewType` makes the annotation itself an error」;
- the header names the failure **as designed**: 「narrow `ViewType` ⇒ the published faces stop accepting `page` ⇒ RED」.

⇒ the spelling is the subject, deleting it destroys the pin, and the repair had to move what checks it. That is the same move objectui#9880 made in the source and objectui#9943 just made for three totals, applied to a fixture.

### ⭐ But the repair is not a transcription of that move — it is sharper, and the seat is recording why

Verified at source, both refs:

```text
main 0564d42e1   PageFaceSkew occurrences: 0      'page' occurrences: 11
head ecec65378   PageFaceSkew occurrences: 8      'page' occurrences: 17   ← the spelling SURVIVED and grew

head :119  type PageFaceSkew<TypeFace extends string, ValueFace extends string> =
     :120    | Exclude<Extract<ValueFace, 'page'>, TypeFace>
     :121    | Exclude<Extract<TypeFace,  'page'>, ValueFace>;
     :124  export type _LivePageFaceSkew = AssertNever<PageFaceSkew<ViewType, ValueFaceViewType>>;
```

That is a symmetric difference restricted to `'page'` over the **two independently derived published faces** — `ViewType` from `SpecListView['type']`, `ValueFaceViewType` from `SpecListViewTypeEnum.options`. So the assert is `never` while both carry `page`, `never` while both drop it, and a **live union the moment either narrows alone**.

⇒ the fixture stops asserting 「`page` is in `ViewType`」 — a claim the retirement is *supposed* to falsify — and starts asserting 「the two faces **agree** about `page`」, which survives the retirement and reddens on skew. ⭐ And the pair it compares is one the zod-mirror ledger **explicitly does not compare**, so this covers a seam nothing else was watching. That is a strictly better pin than the one it replaces, and it is not what the dispatch asked for.

`page`'s bare presence stays asserted literally and at runtime in the sized vocabularies, the `safeParse`, the residual set and the census — so the loudness the card's header promises is preserved, now in seven places rather than one.

### The ablations earn the controls

**A1** reverts to the base blob and the injected leg goes red again at `(146,13)` with the identical TS2322 — restore proven by blob-hash equality **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`. **A2** is the one worth naming: neutralising `PageFaceSkew` so it can only answer `never` produces exactly **two `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`** at the two skew controls ⇒ those controls were suppressing **real** errors, so they are firing rather than decorative. ⛔ A `@ts-expect-error` that nobody has proven fires is a comment, not a control; you proved both.

Keeping the old `pageAsViewType` annotation as a firing control over simulated vocabularies is the right disposal of it — the seat's own read confirms it is still present at head, now as a control rather than as the live assertion.

### Two readings recorded for the family, not for this PR

⚠️ `check:spec-symbols` is **RED under the injected spec** (six hand-written spec-named symbols across four packages, none in this diff) and green on the published one. You flagged it so the injected leg is not misread, and it is exactly what the seat wants on the record: it is a **preview of what objectui#9860's pin bump will surface**, not a defect in this tree today.

And the changeset's empty frontmatter is justified by measurement rather than convention: the only source file is a `*.test.ts` that `packages/core/tsconfig.json` excludes from the emit program, and `packages/core` publishes `["dist","README.md","CHANGELOG.md","LICENSE"]`. Nothing publishable moves.

## Landed — verified by content on `origin/main`

PR objectui#9982 merged at 2026-09-19T01:33:32Z; merge commit `1db82373f767c5331d7ce8d1bfb9beb4420f7cf5`. Reading taken at 2026-09-19T01:36Z against `origin/main` @ `1db82373f` (freshly fetched). `BEFORE` = `8a7e09fa158a01889607b46c855879e99fc29415`, the tip this PR's queue run was built on.

⛔ Verified by CONTENT on both refs, never by sha and never by ancestry. One `git show | grep` pair per row, same path both legs: `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts`.

| reading | BEFORE `8a7e09fa1` | AFTER `1db82373f` |
|---|---|---|
| `'page'` occurrences in the fixture | 11 | **17** |
| `PageFaceSkew` | 0 | **8** |
| CONTROL — `ViewType` (must be lit on BOTH, or the instrument is broken) | 21 | 35 |

⭐ The control is the row that makes the other two readings. `ViewType` is non-zero on both refs, so the file was found and read on both legs; a double zero there would have meant a bad path, not an absent symbol. The card's predicted numbers were `'page'` 11 → 17 and `PageFaceSkew` 0 → present; both landed exactly.

### What the fix actually does

The residual pin no longer **annotates** the `page` face — it **derives** it, and then asserts the derivation is empty:

```ts
type PageFaceSkew<TypeFace extends string, ValueFace extends string> =
  | Exclude<Extract<ValueFace, 'page'>, TypeFace>
  | Exclude<Extract<TypeFace,  'page'>, ValueFace>;

export type _LivePageFaceSkew = AssertNever<PageFaceSkew<ViewType, ValueFaceViewType>>;
```

⭐ Why this is worth more than the count it replaced: it compares two **independently derived** published faces — `ViewType`, read off `SpecListView['type']`, against `ValueFaceViewType`, read off `SpecListViewTypeEnum.options`. That is a pair the zod-mirror ledger explicitly does **not** compare. So the moment the two faces disagree about `page` in either direction, this file stops compiling — and it stops compiling at the seam rather than at a hand-maintained number somebody would have "simplified" on the next pass.

Delivered face, from the merge's own stat: the fixture plus two changesets. ⛔ No product source touched.
